name: creation-grade-2026
summary: Character creation checks the chosen hair, hair colour and face rows for Grade 0 - the 2016 starter style. 2026 renumbered the grades (no 0 at all; starter = 1), so with the 2026 HairInfo / HairColorInfo / FaceInfo every creation from the 2026 client failed with AVATAR_CREATEFAIL 0x183. Make the check Grade == 1.
status: BUILT 2026-09-23. Boot on the stack's Character, then create a character from the 2026 client.
why: Operator, 2026-09-23: character creation from the 2026 client gets no answer at all. The bridge's log showed the
client's NC_AVATAR_CREATE_REQ answered by NC_AVATAR_CREATEFAIL_ACK err 0x0183 in 17 ms, three times.
Character.exe's reply builder (0x404B30) maps the create worker's result: >0 success, -1 -> 0x182, -2 -> 0x183,
-3 -> 0x184, else 0x181. The worker (0x404280) returns -2 at 0x404B09 from exactly one place before it ever
reaches the database - the appearance check. It looks the chosen hair, colour and face up (HairInfo holder
0x6EC870, HairColorInfo 0x6EC830, FaceInfo 0x6EC7F0, each a row lookup by id through 0x43FDC0), requires each
row to exist, and then:
0x4043A6  cmp byte [ecx+0x3D], bl ; jne fail     HairColorInfo.Grade      (bl = 0 in this function)
0x4043AF  cmp byte [edx+0x41], bl ; jne fail     HairInfo.Grade
0x4043B8  cmp byte [eax+0x21], bl ; jne fail     FaceInfo.Grade
The offsets are the Grade column in each in-memory row - the style-change handler (0x4182B0) reads the same three
offsets as the grade that picks a style ticket. Replayed with the exact values the client sent, p_Char_Create
itself succeeds; only this check refuses.
2016 grades: 0 = starter (creatable), 1 = ?, 4 / 5 = shop tiers. 2026 grades: 1 = starter (20 hairs, 10 colours,
20 faces), 4 / 5 / 6 = shop tiers - there is no 0 anywhere, and 2026 promoted some 2016 shop styles to starter
(Face 20: 2016 grade 4, 2026 grade 1). The 2026 client offers exactly its grade-1 rows on the creation screen.
The operator's call: use the 2026 tables as they are and make the exe speak 2026.
THE PATCH rewrites the 27 bytes in place - no cave - comparing with 1 instead of bl, with short jumps to one
shared fail stub:
cmp byte [ecx+0x3D],1 ; jne stub ; cmp byte [edx+0x41],1 ; jne stub ; cmp byte [eax+0x21],1 ; je 0x4043C1
stub: jmp 0x404B09 ; nop x4
Nothing after 0x4043C1 reads the flags, and the register state is unchanged (the compares only read memory).
NOT CHANGED, and why it is still right: the style-change path (0x4182B0) derives a ticket item as
base + max(grade) - 1, with grade 0 treated as 1. So 2026 grades 1 / 4 / 5 pick exactly the tickets 2016's
0-1 / 4 / 5 did. 2026's new tier 6 reaches base + 5, a ticket 2016 never used - see the ticket in
Fiesta2026on2016's tickets.md.
CONSEQUENCE: with the 2026 tables there are no Grade-0 rows, so a 2016 CLIENT's creation screen (which lists
grade 0) offers no hair, colour or face. The 2026 client is the target; the merged 2016 client is not.
